mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and lowers the cost of capital for corporations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved valuation metrics.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals monetary tightening, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market expansion (HOUST > 1300 thousand units), rising consumer credit (RSAFS) signals strong household spending that drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST > 1300, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS rises.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production index (INDPRO) above 110 reflects robust manufacturing output and capacity utilization, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above 110.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate below 3.5% indicates a tight labor market that increases wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 2% in the prior quarter signals sustained economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth (quarter-over-quarter) exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing market (HOUST > 1300 thousand units) combined with moderate inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%) indicates stable consumer demand and price environment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1300 and CPIAUCSL < 2.5%.
